name: Kalser Glocknerstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Kalser Glocknerstraße leads to the Lucknerhaus with the most impressive direct view of Austria's highest peak, the Großglockner (3,798 m).
dauer: Half-day excursion (approx. 2 to 4 hours, including short hike)
preis: Car toll approx. €12.00 per day; discount available with the Osttirol guest card
oeffnungszeiten: Mid-May to late October open daily (subject to weather conditions)
beschreibung:
Overview

The magnificent Kalser Glocknerstraße in the East Tyrolean Hohe Tauern National Park guides nature lovers and mountain enthusiasts directly to the base of Austria's highest mountain. Over a stretch of roughly seven kilometers, the toll-paying panoramic road winds from the tranquil national park village of Kals am Großglockner (1,324 m) up to the historic mountain inn Lucknerhaus at 1,920 meters above sea level. At the end of the road, an iconic postcard panorama opens onto the pyramid peak of the Großglockner (3,798 m), framed by rushing glacial torrents, lush pastures, and ancient stone pine forests. Unlike the heavily visited Großglockner High Alpine Road, this route has preserved its quiet, pristine, and peaceful high-mountain ambiance.

Route & Requirements

The road is asphalted, wide, and features a gentle maximum gradient of ten percent, making it suitable for cars, motorbikes, and small buses. At Lucknerhaus, spacious parking areas provide a convenient starting point for hikes of all abilities. A popular family-friendly walk follows a broad gravel track for about an hour up to rustic Lucknerhütte (2,241 m) in the Ködnitztal; stronger hikers can continue for two more hours to Stüdlhütte (2,801 m), the base for summit climbs of the Großglockner. For valley walks, sturdy walking shoes with profiled soles suffice, while routes above Lucknerhütte require high-alpine equipment and surefootedness. Information boards and mounted telescopes along the paths make it easy to spot marmots, chamois, golden eagles, and bearded vultures.

Visit & Arrival

The Kalser Glocknerstraße is open to public traffic during snow-free months from mid-May to late October (in winter, limited access to lower car parks only). The toll fee is around €12.00 per car; discounts apply for guests staying in Kals with a valid guest card. Drivers reach East Tyrol via the Felbertauern road or via the Drau Valley and Lienz, turning off at Huben into the Kalser Valley. In summer, national park buses run regularly between Lienz, Kals, and Lucknerhaus.

Tips

Visit the viewing deck right by Lucknerhaus in the early morning when the sunrise illuminates the summit cross of the Großglockner with golden light. Enjoy homemade East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen ravioli with chive butter on the sunny terrace of Lucknerhaus.
